source: NCERT Class VIII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 5.

sections.heading: 1. Force
points: A **force** is a **push or pull** on an object, arising from an interaction; measured in **newtons (N)**.

sub: Start or stop motion; change **speed** or **direction**; change **shape**.

points: A **net (unbalanced) force** changes an object's state of motion; **balanced forces** do not.

sections.heading: 2. Contact and Non-contact Forces
points: **Non-contact forces** (act at a distance): **gravitational, magnetic, electrostatic** forces.
**Gravity** pulls all objects towards the Earth (gives them **weight**).

sections.heading: 3. Pressure
points: A **smaller area gives more pressure** (sharp knife, nail); a **larger area gives less** (wide straps, camel's feet).
**Liquids and gases exert pressure** that **increases with depth**; **atmospheric pressure** is the weight of air, balanced by pressure inside our body.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Force = push/pull (newton); changes speed, direction or shape.
Balanced forces = no change in motion; unbalanced (net) force = change.
Contact: muscular, friction; non-contact: gravity, magnetic, electrostatic.
Pressure = Force ÷ Area (pascal); smaller area → more pressure.
Liquid/gas pressure increases with depth; atmospheric pressure = weight of air.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Pressure = Force ÷ Area** — a smaller area gives more pressure.
**Balanced forces** cause **no change** in motion; only an **unbalanced** force does.
**Weight** is the force of gravity on an object.
